claims.text: Equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has low hardness and strength despite good plasticity.
CoCrFeNiTi forms a stable, chemically disordered single-phase solid solution.
The chemically disordered single-phase state permits nearly unimpeded dislocation glide in CoCrFeNiTi.
CoCrFeNiTi lacks significant early-stage obstacles such as deformation twins, precipitates, and strain-induced phase transformations.
Twinning, transformation, nanoscale particles, and related evolving microstructures can increase strength in other high-entropy alloys without necessarily sacrificing ductility.
A low resistance to dislocation motion causes the reduced yield strength and hardness of CoCrFeNiTi while retaining plasticity.
The proposed starting material has relatively coarse grains and minimal pre-existing obstacles or short-range order.
Uniaxial tensile testing and nanoindentation combined with TEM or EBSD can be used to test the proposed mechanism.
Dynamic recovery is active and thermally activated recovery dominates in CoCrFeNiTi at room temperature and low-to-moderate strain rates.
A homogeneous matrix lacking precipitates, twin boundaries, and transformation products presents few internal barriers to dislocation glide.
The simple solid solution in CoCrFeNiTi provides a low-lattice-friction environment.
Nearly unhindered dislocation motion promotes plasticity but prevents the buildup of internal stresses needed for hardening.
Low stacking-fault energy, or a lack of driving force for additional defect interactions, enables dynamic recovery and smooth dislocation motion.
Mechanical testing should reveal low yield strength, low hardness, low strain-hardening rates, and uniform plastic deformation.
In situ characterization should show predominant dislocation glide with little deformation-induced twinning or phase transformation.
An FCC-to-HCP transformation can strengthen a related alloy through an evolving deformation-induced microstructure.
The hypothesis may cease to apply at very high strain rates or cryogenic temperatures because alternative deformation mechanisms could be activated.
Short-range ordering or incipient precipitation may occur during deformation and modify dislocation interactions.
The FCC-versus-BCC structure of CoCrFeNiTi may modulate the available slip behavior.

Observation of significant deformation twinning, a strain-induced phase transformation, or substantially greater-than-predicted work hardening would falsify the proposed unobstructed-glide explanation.

contradictions.description: The mechanism invokes low stacking-fault energy as enabling smooth glide and dynamic recovery, whereas low stacking-fault energy is also commonly associated with enhanced faulting, twinning, or transformation—the very mechanisms predicted to be absent. The hypothesis does not resolve this tension or specify which alternative applies.
